Explanation: It is time to say goodbye to NASA 's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory . After nearly 22 years of service, the satellite re-entered Earth's atmosphere on November 4 at 7:39 EST over the North Sumatra region of Indonesia .

The featured image is a mosaic created in 2018 using the first one million images captured by the satellite's Ultraviolet/Optical Telescope . Swift had a combination of instruments, including an X-ray telescope and a gamma-ray telescope , that worked together to enable humanity to study, in unprecedented detail, the fastest and most energetic explosions in the universe. The most recent solar maximum accelerated the decay of the satellite's orbit.

An innovative mission to rescue Swift by boosting its orbit was not successful . Swift burned on reentry like a shooting star, but the impressive data acquired by the telescope over its mission will continue to bring light to the mysteries of the cosmos for years to come. May it keep inspiring new missions to boldly go into space, explore new data and seek out new science.

The San Juan River has carved deep, improbably curvy meanders into the desert landscape. Tens of millions of years ago, the San Juan River in what is now southern Utah shared some characteristics with today's Mississippi River. Today, on its westward path to Lake Powell, the San Juan River flows through an impressive series of entrenched meanders, also known as “goosenecks.” An astronaut aboard the International Space Station photographed the stark desert topography on October 6, 2026.

In Utah’s Goosenecks State Park , the river runs through a canyon 1,000 feet (300 meters) deep. Goosenecks State Park’s remote, high-desert location and 360-degree views of the sky helped earn it an International Dark Sky Park designation in 2021. The WANDRD Magnetic Camera Strap comes in three different sizes and three different colors. articles.summary_long:
Le Nikon Film Festival a dévoilé ce vendredi 6 novembre le nom du président du jury de sa 17e édition : Orelsan . Le rappeur et réalisateur succède à Nathan Ambrosioni, et l’annonce s’accompagne de la création d’un prix dédié à la musique originale . Orelsan, de son vrai nom Aurélien Cotentin, aura la charge de départager, avec le reste du jury, les courts-métrages et mini-séries de cette 17e édition, dont le palmarès sera dévoilé le 22 avril 2027 au Grand Rex, à Paris.

Le festival profite de l’annonce pour créer un Prix de la Musique Originale , qui récompensera les compositeurs et compositrices des films et mini-séries en compétition. Dévoilé cet été, le thème de cette 17e édition tient en un mot : « Surprise » . Il succède à « La beauté » , qui avait porté l’édition 2026 à un record de 3 255 films (2 577 courts-métrages et 113 mini-séries de six épisodes), dont 42 % réalisés par des femmes, avant un Grand Prix du Jury remis à L’Éclat de Tansi Makele.

Deux formats sont proposés : un ou plusieurs courts-métrages de 2 min 20, ou une mini-série de six épisodes de 2 min 20 reliés par un fil narratif. La sélection officielle sera annoncée le 1er avril et le palmarès remis le 22 avril au Grand Rex. Retrouvez l’ensemble de nos articles consacrés au festival sur notre page dédiée au Nikon Film Festival .

La v2.00 va plus loin, et Nikon la présente comme la première mise à jour majeure de la caméra.

En Log3G10 comme en N-Log, on peut choisir parmi quatre niveaux de réduction du bruit en haute sensibilité. Côté mise au point, le focus peaking arrive enfin en R3D NE, y compris quand un LUT 3D est appliqué. Nikon n’annonce en revanche aucune évolution de l’autofocus avec cette version.

En septembre, Nikon avait aussi indiqué que RED mettait à jour ses applications de pilotage à distance RED Control et RED Control Pro pour les rendre compatibles avec la ZR. Nikon annonce que le firmware 2.00 sortira avant la fin de 2026 , sans date précise pour l’instant. Pour en savoir plus sur la caméra, retrouvez notre prise en main de la Nikon ZR et notre interview Nikon à l’IBC 2025 .

Après une campagne Kickstarter qui a dépassé les espérances de ses créateurs, Mondo Robotics ouvre les ventes de Beni , un robot caméra sur roues capable de suivre son utilisateur et de le filmer en 4K , sans opérateur ni trépied. Contrairement aux drones à suivi automatique de DJI, Beni ne vole pas : il roule au sol, aux côtés de son sujet. Les premières livraisons sont annoncées à partir du 10 novembre 2026 , et le robot est proposé dès 841 dollars (environ 730 €) en prix de lancement pour la France.

Beni est le premier produit de Mondo Robotics , une jeune entreprise fondée en 2025 et basée à Hong Kong , qui revendique environ 150 ingénieurs et designers répartis entre Shenzhen et Palo Alto et une équipe en partie issue de DJI . Face à une caméra de poche stabilisée comme la DJI Osmo Pocket 4P et son double objectif, Beni apporte l’autonomie de déplacement , au prix d’un encombrement et d’un tarif bien supérieurs . Au-delà de son allure de petit robot de dessin animé, Beni embarque un module caméra comparable à celui des caméras de poche récentes.

Beni n’est pas étanche , Mondo Robotics le réserve donc aux usages par temps sec. Mondo Robotics, malgré une équipe en partie issue de chez DJI, en est à son premier produit . Peut-être que c’est celui-ci que l’équipe de Mondo Robotics a repris… Enfin, la législation reste floue.

articles.title: OpenAI dévoile GPT-6 Cyber
articles.summary: Spécialisé dans la cybersécurité et réservé à un cercle restreint de clients, GPT-6 Cyber vise à faciliter la détection et l'analyse des vulnérabilités logicielles. OpenAI revendique notamment la découverte de 81 failles inédites de haute gravité dans Firefox.
articles.summary_short: Spécialisé dans la cybersécurité et réservé à un cercle restreint de clients, GPT-6 Cyber vise à faciliter la détection et l'analyse des vulnérabilités logicielles. OpenAI revendique notamment la découverte de 81 failles inédites de haute gravité dans Firefox.
articles.summary_long:
Spécialisé dans la cybersécurité et réservé à un cercle restreint de clients, GPT-6 Cyber vise à faciliter la détection et l'analyse des vulnérabilités logicielles. OpenAI revendique notamment la découverte de 81 failles inédites de haute gravité dans Firefox. Quelques jours après avoir dévoilé Image 2.6, la nouvelle version de son générateur d'images, OpenAI annonce GPT-6 Cyber, un modèle spécialisé dans la cybersécurité et dérivé de GPT-6 Astra.

OpenAI poursuit le développement de ses capacités en cybersécurité avec GPT-6 Cyber, une déclinaison spécialisée de son modèle GPT-6 Astra. Les premiers résultats communiqués par OpenAI illustrent les capacités du modèle. Lors de travaux menés sur Firefox, GPT-6 Cyber a permis d’identifier 81 vulnérabilités inédites, classées de haute gravité par Mozilla.

Le modèle aurait permis de reproduire 1 724 vulnérabilités et de développer 948 exploits fonctionnels. OpenAI classe ce modèle au niveau « critique » en matière de cybersécurité, une première pour ses modèles Cyber. GPT-6 Cyber n’est donc pas proposé en accès libre.

articles.summary_long:
Rocky planetesimals were whizzing around in the Solar System back then, and Earth formed as more of these objects collided and merged with it. Some of these collisions were giant impacts that generated immense heat. Planetary scientists have wondered how young planets like Earth could've held onto their atmospheres near the end of their accretion period.

The island of Cyprus began to form some 90 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous , with molten rock pouring from the seafloor, solidifying, and building new oceanic crust . Remnants of that ancient island are still visible in the dark rocks of the Troodos Mountains .

During the Miocene , considerably younger layers of chalk, limestone, marl, and other marine sedimentary rocks accumulated around the island, providing material that developed into a second, smaller island to the south during a later period of geologic uplift . On Wednesday, NASA unveiled its newest experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, during the UP.Summit at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. This high-performance, highly adaptable research platform is designed to accelerate the development and testing of advanced aviation technologies. The crewed X-70 features advanced, rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology that will allow NASA to explore aircraft maneuverability in ways never before demonstrated in crewed flight.

The aircraft can also accommodate up to 2,000 pounds of experimental payloads in internal and external locations, enabling a wide range of research and flight-testing opportunities. “The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. These capabilities will enable NASA to conduct demanding flight research across a broad range of operating conditions.

“For decades, NASA Aeronautics has used X-planes to develop technologies that advance aviation,” said Laurie Grindle, director of the Aeronautics Division within NASA’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate. With the X-70, NASA will expand its capacity to conduct experimental flight research, accelerate the testing of emerging technologies, and advance the next generation of American aviation. NASA successfully demonstrated technology designed to help spacecraft autonomously navigate to safe landing sites on the Moon and on other planets. An Alta-X drone equipped with the agency’s Safe and Precise Landing – Integrated Capabilities Evolution ( SPLICE ) guidance, navigation, and control payload completed simulated lunar descent and landing maneuvers Aug. The flight took place at Rogers Dry Lake near NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California.

During the tests, the SPLICE payload used an advanced guidance system to map the terrain and assess potential landing areas. If the system determines the targeted landing area is unsafe, the system diverts the drone to a safer location. “This flight test is the culmination of almost a decade of work, for the SPLICE project,” said Davis Adams, NASA project manager.

Validation of the guidance and navigation systems are applicable to terrestrial, lunar, and Martian descent and landing missions.” NASA has worked with a number of commercial lunar lander providers to implement iterations of SPLICE into their platforms. “Some of the companies also are evaluating the system’s navigation capabilities for precision landing applications, as well as potential extensions for autonomous surface mobility.” NASA’s Flight Opportunities project, based at NASA Armstrong, enabled flight testing of the SPLICE project early in its development that laid a foundation for it to continue advancing its technology readiness level to what it is today. Flight testing included both a descent altitude and a landing trajectory in 2019 similar to what is expected on a lunar mission and the demonstration of two NASA-developed precision landing sensor systems in 2020.

In the last week of December 2010, a railroad worker named Jim DeNike drove from Arkansas to Parsons, Kansas, and loaded a dozen boxes holding nearly 50,000 slides into an old maroon Pontiac. He had sent Dwayne's Photo 1,580 rolls of Kodachrome and paid $15,798 to have them developed, borrowing against his father's retirement account to cover it. Kodachrome died when one small lab in southeast Kansas went quiet, because a Kodachrome roll was not a color film in any sense a modern photographer would recognize.

Nearly every other color film you have shot carries its couplers inside the emulsion, waiting for oxidized developer to meet them and form dye in place. The yellow developer then builds yellow dye in the top layer. The middle green-sensitive layer gets no light at all.

The film only becomes a color film at the end of that chain, and the chain was scrapped in Parsons in January 2011. You can still find frozen Kodachrome on auction sites, and you can still shoot it. The one machine it cannot run is the one that made Kodachrome a color film, and there are 50,000 slides of trains in Arkansas that exist because one man got them to Kansas in time.

articles.title: High-Speed Sync vs. Global Shutter for Flash Portraits in Bright Sun
articles.summary: Sony's a9 III and its global shutter offer a way past that wall, which puts high-speed sync, the usual workaround, in an interesting spot. For high-speed sync, the flash sat at 5.2.
articles.summary_short: Sony's a9 III and its global shutter offer a way past that wall, which puts high-speed sync, the usual workaround, in an interesting spot. For high-speed sync, the flash sat at 5.2.
articles.summary_long:
Shoot a flash portrait at f/1.2 in midday sun and you run into a wall fast: most cameras stop syncing with a flash somewhere around 1/160 to 1/250 s, and anything faster leaves dark bands across the frame. Sony's a9 III and its global shutter offer a way past that wall, which puts high-speed sync, the usual workaround, in an interesting spot. The high-speed sync shots come from a Sony a7R VI with the Sony FE 50mm f/1.2 GM , because the Sony a9 III won't go into high-speed sync mode at all.

At f/1.2, the ceiling drops to 1/16,000 s, which is still far beyond what a focal plane shutter can sync at. For high-speed sync, the flash sat at 5.2. The logic carries over to leaf shutter cameras such as the Fujifilm X100VI , where the flash also fires as one burst at shutter speeds a focal plane shutter can't sync at.

On any camera, shutter speed sets how bright the background looks, and the flash sets how bright your subject looks. A global or leaf shutter lets you push those two apart much further. What the global shutter opens up for portraits is control over ambient light.

At the turn of the 20th century, art—especially the “high” mediums of painting and sculpture—were viewed and taught through the lens of deeply ingrained conventions about what made art good.

Chief among these was representation: people look like people, landscapes look like landscapes, and rooms look like rooms. That is, until Henri Matisse created “ The Red Studio .” A prized painting in MoMA’s collection in New York, “The Red Studio,” or “L’Atelier rouge,” was so unexpected that, according to a wonderful new video from Great Art Explained , Matisse may not have really been able to grasp what he’d done either, at least not right away. “The painting seemed to break almost every established rule of Western painting,” Payne says.

Avast déploie en France un VPN gratuit, sans publicité et utilisable sur un nombre illimité d'appareils. L'éditeur de cybersécurité mise sur une formule sans plafond de données pour se démarquer de ses concurrents, tout en réservant certaines fonctionnalités à son offre payante. Avast lance en France une nouvelle offre VPN gratuite, accessible sur Windows, macOS, Android et iOS.

Avast annonce également l'absence de publicité et de plafond mensuel de données. Avast propose aussi une fonctionnalité permettant de suspendre temporairement le VPN pendant 15, 30 ou 60 minutes. Les utilisateurs peuvent sélectionner trois emplacements de serveurs, contre davantage de destinations avec l'abonnement Avast Premium VPN.

L'éditeur indique également que sa formule gratuite propose des vitesses standard. La décision interdit notamment à Avast de vendre ou de concéder sous licence des données de navigation à des fins publicitaires. Le marché compte déjà des offres gratuites, notamment celle de Proton VPN.

articles.title: Assyria is Far from Ancient in Esther Elia’s Characterizations of Contemporary ‘Diasporic Deities’
articles.summary: Across ancient Mesopotamia, lamassu figures assumed the form of a winged goddess. She adds: The home is where our language is spoken.
articles.summary_short: Across ancient Mesopotamia, lamassu figures assumed the form of a winged goddess. She adds: The home is where our language is spoken.
articles.summary_long:
Across ancient Mesopotamia, lamassu figures assumed the form of a winged goddess. In the ancient Assyrian Empire, giant bulls or lions with human heads and wings represented the deities, which artisans often carved at a monumental scale to protect cities and palaces. For Albuquerque-based Esther Elia , who is of Assyrian and Irish descent, lamassu are anything but a relic of the distant past.

Through sculpture, paintings, and textiles, the artist explores contemporary Assyrian experience through pattern, fashion, and autobiography. Her solo exhibition, Bazaar Ashuraya at Hecho a Mano , centers around a new collection of acrylic paintings, plus tile mosaics and functional objects. Elia delves into the theme of home, where lamps, garments, and paintings evocative of rugs or tapestries portray vibrant figures, shapes, and objects associated with daily life.

“The home is where Assyria lives and breathes,” Elia says in a statement. She adds: The home is where our language is spoken. Even if we speak English or Arabic or Farsi or French or Swedish outside of the home, the home is where Assyrian food is made, where Assyrian customs thrive, and where culture is maintained as well as created—pushed forward.

articles.summary_long:
From California to Oklahoma to Illinois, Black communities are saddling up and grasping the reins of a horse or ornery bull. A thriving culture that’s gained attention in recent years, these competitors form bonds in and out of the rodeo arena, where their animals kick up dust and barrel across the ring. Since 2015, photographer Ivan McClellan has been embedded within these communities across the U.S.

His new book, Eight Seconds: Legacy in Motion , is an addendum to his earlier body of work with 91 new images that spotlight the people and places integral to Black rodeo culture. Published by Damiani , the updated edition features Texan teenager Kortnee Solomon, who’s captivated audiences as one of the youngest competitors, on the cover. Flanked by horses, Solomon stands proudly wearing a rainbow-colored money shirt and blue hat, her eyes shaded by the brim.

Additional images zoom into the arena alongside cowboys racing across the dirt stage and toward the stands, where the audience cheers under the bright, stadium lights. Find both the earlier and new edition on Bookshop. Find a larger archive of McClellan’s work on his website and Instagram .

Raised in Nigeria’s Kaduna region, Obijiaku recently moved to Chicago, where he has grappled with the emotional resonance of distance and getting used to an entirely new place.

“Seen through a sentimental lens, these settings lend the paintings an intimate, dreamlike quality, as though recalling a presence from memory,” says a statement from Roberts Projects , which will be presenting the artist’s forthcoming solo show, Wherever You Are, Remember Me . Obijiaku relishes how everyday experiences have the potential to prompt memories. Sounds can transport us to specific times and places in our past.

And when exploring somewhere new, it’s common to experience a kind of illusory familiarity, such as when a stranger passes on the street and they remind us of someone we objectively know is thousands of miles away. “Rengaji,” for example, nods to Renaissance paintings in the Christian tradition of the likes of Fra Angelico , while also referencing Obijiaku’s own childhood memories of royal processions in Nigeria, where crowds would gather to observe the king. Après une première série de piratages en France en octobre, les systèmes de réfrigération de plusieurs enseignes européennes ont de nouveau été ciblés ce 2 novembre. Belgique, Suède, Irlande et plusieurs autres pays sont concernés. Lundi 2 novembre, les installations frigorifiques de plusieurs supermarchés européens ont été manipulées à distance, provoquant des pertes de marchandises et des perturbations opérationnelles.

Plusieurs enseignes européennes ont signalé des dysfonctionnements de leurs équipements de réfrigération. En Belgique, une quarantaine de magasins Delhaize auraient été touchés, tandis que plusieurs points de vente Carrefour ont également signalé des incidents. Des magasins Intermarché et Spar figurent aussi parmi les établissements concernés.

La Suède et l'Irlande sont également affectées, l'enseigne ICA a confirmé des incidents dans plusieurs magasins, tandis qu'au moins treize supermarchés SuperValu ont confirmé la perte de produits frais et surgelés. Le Luxembourg, les Pays-Bas et l'Estonie figurent aussi parmi les pays concernés. Environ 700 magasins auraient été concernés par la compromission de leurs systèmes de réfrigération.

articles.summary_long:
Astrophysicists think that the supermassive black holes (SMBH) we see in the modern Universe are the result of a long drawn-out process. That process is referred to as the hierarchical black hole mergers framework. Some of the most massive appear to have billions of solar masses.

They either explode as supernovae, and their cores collapse, forming black holes, or they collapse directly into black holes. In between stellar mass black holes and SMBH are intermediate mass black holes (IMBH.) These black holes range in mass from about 100 solar masses to 100,000 solar masses. A 2020 paper presented the only direct evidence of an IMBH when the waves showed that two black holes, with 85 and 66 solar masses, merged to create an IMBH with about 142 solar masses.

Research titled " Massive star clusters detected by JWST as natural birth places to form intermediate-mass black holes " may have the answer. articles.title: Researchers May Have Solved a Puzzling Contradiction in the Ryugu Sample
articles.summary: Asteroids are critically different than their planetary counterparts. (Courtesy: JAXA) There's obviously no soil on Ryugu, but there is aqueous alteration.
articles.summary_short: Asteroids are critically different than their planetary counterparts. (Courtesy: JAXA) There's obviously no soil on Ryugu, but there is aqueous alteration.
articles.summary_long:
The Solar System's asteroids are sometimes referred to as fossils because they preserve evidence of the conditions when the Solar System formed. Asteroids are critically different than their planetary counterparts. Aqueous alteration isn't a rare action that happens only in space environments; it's common on Earth.

(Courtesy: JAXA) There's obviously no soil on Ryugu, but there is aqueous alteration. There seems to be two components, each altered under a different set of aqueous conditions. An asteroid can be clumpy on a macroscale, but how can it have two components in the same mineral matrix?

They found the expected serpentine and saponite, but they also identified something else: poorly crystalline magnesium silicate hydrate (M-S-H). Much of their matrices could be poorly crystalline M-S-H. That sample should be on Earth five years from now.

articles.title: In 2013, Researchers Pulled Recognizable Faces of Bystanders Out of the Eye Reflections in a Portrait
articles.summary: The face was a reflection in another person's eye. A 102-megapixel file puts you about 3.5 times above it.
articles.summary_short: The face was a reflection in another person's eye. A 102-megapixel file puts you about 3.5 times above it.
articles.summary_long:
An anonymous peer reviewer worked through a manuscript, looked at one of its figures, and recognized one of the authors. The face was a reflection in another person's eye. The subject's face, hair excluded, took up about 12 million of them.

The iris took about 54,000, which the authors note is under 0.5% of frontal face area. Out of that iris, they cropped rectangles 27 to 36 pixels wide by 42 to 56 pixels high, framed head and shoulders like a tiny passport photo. Average face area inside those crops was 322 pixels.

At identical framing, a bystander crop that ran 27 to 36 pixels wide in 2013 comes out around 44 to 58 pixels wide today, and 322 pixels of face area becomes about 839. A 102-megapixel file puts you about 3.5 times above it. The GFX100 II's pixel pitch works out to 43.8 mm across 11,648 pixels, or 3.76 micrometers.

articles.title: Jeffrey Gibson’s ‘A Real Love Thing’ Surveys a Decade of the Artist’s Multidisciplinary Practice
articles.summary: Through abstract, prismatic acrylic paintings to garment-like sculptures and textile collages, Jeffrey Gibson explores questions of identity, lineage, and cultural translation. Working across media, the artist intricately beads monumental works and incorporates a wide range of fabrics and materials.
articles.summary_short: Through abstract, prismatic acrylic paintings to garment-like sculptures and textile collages, Jeffrey Gibson explores questions of identity, lineage, and cultural translation. articles.summary_long:
Through abstract, prismatic acrylic paintings to garment-like sculptures and textile collages, Jeffrey Gibson explores questions of identity, lineage, and cultural translation. Working across media, the artist intricately beads monumental works and incorporates a wide range of fabrics and materials. Jeffrey Gibson: A Real Love Thing at Johns Hopkins University Bloomberg Center delves into the cross-disciplinary breadth of the artist’s practice throughout the past decade.

Drawing on the early and continuing influence of music, the artist often integrates song lyrics into tapestry-like wall hangings and three-dimensional works. Music also inspired the title of the exhibition, which Gibson drew from a 1971 interview with soul artist Marvin Gaye, who described his seminal album What’s Going On by saying, “I think I’ve got a real love thing going. I love people, I love life, and I love nature, and I can’t see why other people can’t be like that.” Reflecting this sentiment, Gibson’s approach is a luminous celebration of Indigenous symbolism and traditional materials, such as jingle cones used in ceremonial garments, tipi poles, and glass beads that have coated bags, moccasins, and other apparel hand-crafted by Native Americans throughout the centuries.

The artist also posits a future full of hope, joy, acceptance, and, like Gaye, a love-above-all ethos. A Real Love Thing continues through March 13 at the Bloomberg Center in Washington, D.C., where Gibson will present a talk as part of the esteemed Sam Gilliam Lecture series on November 12. And if you’re near Eugene, Oregon, the artist’s traveling solo exhibition They Teach Love is also on view through through March 7 at the University of Oregon.

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Explanation: What’s causing this unusually long cloud on Mars ? Known as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC) and first recorded by NASA’s Viking Orbiter 2 in 1977, the strange cloud has been imaged in greater detail more recently by ESA ’s robotic Mars Express spacecraft.

The cloud forms only during spring and summer seasons and then only during morning hours. Made of water-ice, the most familiar process that causes cloud crystals to form around bits of dust would fail due to the thinness and lack of dust high in the Martian atmosphere . Leading speculation holds that dust is not involved.

After the cloud forms near the volcano Arsia Mons , wind blows the cloud downstream — creating a tail that can extend over 1500 kilometers. Efforts to better understand AMEC s will continue, an understanding that may bolster a more complete view of cloud formation on Earth .

articles.title: Binance victime d'un vol de cryptomonnaies de 6,3 Md$
articles.summary: L'enquête préliminaire évoque la compromission d'un ordinateur portable appartenant à un ingénieur DevOps. Si aucune fuite de clés privées n'a été identifiée à ce stade, les investigations ont depuis mis au jour plusieurs points de compromission.
articles.summary_short: L'enquête préliminaire évoque la compromission d'un ordinateur portable appartenant à un ingénieur DevOps. Si aucune fuite de clés privées n'a été identifiée à ce stade, les investigations ont depuis mis au jour plusieurs points de compromission.
articles.summary_long:
L'enquête préliminaire évoque la compromission d'un ordinateur portable appartenant à un ingénieur DevOps. Si aucune fuite de clés privées n'a été identifiée à ce stade, les investigations ont depuis mis au jour plusieurs points de compromission. Le montant dérobé dépasse largement celui du précédent grand vol de cryptomonnaies, estimé à 1,5 Md$ lors de l'attaque contre Bybit en février 2025.

D'après les premières investigations communiquées par Binance, l'attaque pourrait avoir commencé par la compromission de l'ordinateur portable d'un ingénieur DevOps de l'entreprise. Les sociétés spécialisées dans l'analyse de la blockchain, notamment TRM Labs et Chainalysis, ont établi des liens entre cette attaque et le groupe de pirates TraderTraitor, associé à la Corée du Nord. Ce groupe est déjà soupçonné d'être impliqué dans plusieurs opérations de vol de cryptomonnaies à grande échelle.

Face à l'ampleur de l'attaque, plusieurs acteurs majeurs de l'écosystème financier numérique ont rapidement réagi. Tether, Circle et Ripple ont notamment participé au gel d'une partie des actifs dérobés. Cependant, plusieurs milliards de dollars restent difficiles à récupérer, notamment lorsque les pirates convertissent les actifs en cryptomonnaies qui ne peuvent pas être gelées directement par un émetteur centralisé.

articles.title: Martian Polar Crater Ice Shifts with Seasonal Frost
articles.summary: The planet Mars shares many landforms and weather patterns with the Earth, including changing seasons, volcanoes, canyons, dust storms and dust devils, and water ice. But one feature that Earth and Mars share among the eight planets in our solar system are polar ice caps.
articles.summary_short: The planet Mars shares many landforms and weather patterns with the Earth, including changing seasons, volcanoes, canyons, dust storms and dust devils, and water ice. But one feature that Earth and Mars share among the eight planets in our solar system are polar ice caps.
articles.summary_long:
The planet Mars shares many landforms and weather patterns with the Earth, including changing seasons, volcanoes, canyons, dust storms and dust devils, and water ice. But one feature that Earth and Mars share among the eight planets in our solar system are polar ice caps. Both are one of each planetâs striking features, but the major difference is while Earthâs polar ice caps are both comprised of water, Marsâ north polar ice cap is only comprised of water while its southern polar ice cap is carbon dioxide.

But how does the north polar ice cap water ice change with the seasons compared to Earth, and what can this teach scientists about Marsâ climate history? As discussed in a recent study published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Planets, the researchers challenged our understanding of ice deposits in Marsâ northern polar ice cap region. The researchers note that better understanding seasonal changes in polar ice cap deposits could help gain insights into long-term climate changes on the Red Planet.

For the study, the researchers analyzed images of 36 craters within the northern polar ice cap region of Mars. This study identifies seasonal changes in polar ice deposits while providing motivation for future modeling work that could help expand our understanding of localized climates on Mars. What new insights into Mars polar crater ice will researchers make in the coming years and decades?

articles.summary: The finding resolves an existing paradox about how salt-rich deposits arise in the Ceres near-surface; they are likely not initially salt-rich but instead result from enrichment of salt at the optical surface by sublimation of salty ices.â Essentially, the salt-water ice deposits are sorted based on heat and evaporation, the salt within water ice mixture causes the water ice to evaporate faster, leaving behind the salt deposits. Instead, they start out with low amounts of salt but have their salt contents increase from the evaporation of water ice that also contains salt.
articles.summary_short: The finding resolves an existing paradox about how salt-rich deposits arise in the Ceres near-surface; they are likely not initially salt-rich but instead result from enrichment of salt at the optical surface by sublimation of salty ices.â Essentially, the salt-water ice deposits are sorted based on heat and evaporation, the salt within water ice mixture causes the water ice to evaporate faster, leaving behind the salt deposits. articles.summary_long:
The dwarf planet Ceres is arguably one of the most overlooked and underappreciated planetary objects in the entire solar system. This could be because while Ceres has the same dwarf planet designation as Pluto, Ceres is largely considered an âasteroidâ since it resides the in main asteroid belt. For the study, researchers used a combination of Dawn spacecraft data and a series of computer models to examine the evolution of surface water ice and salt deposits on Ceresâ surface.

Specifically, this study focused on the transition of water ice to salt deposits through evaporation (scientifically called sublimation) and whether data collected from Dawn accurately estimated the amount of water ice and salt. In the end, the researchers found that the salt deposits might be hidden by the water ice deposits theyâre mixed with, with the salt deposits potentially existing in larger amounts than previously hypothesized, estimated to be between 30 to 50 percent greater. The finding resolves an existing paradox about how salt-rich deposits arise in the Ceres near-surface; they are likely not initially salt-rich but instead result from enrichment of salt at the optical surface by sublimation of salty ices.â Essentially, the salt-water ice deposits are sorted based on heat and evaporation, the salt within water ice mixture causes the water ice to evaporate faster, leaving behind the salt deposits.

This creates a feedback loop that results in different mixture amounts and types among separate water ice and salt deposits. Instead, they start out with low amounts of salt but have their salt contents increase from the evaporation of water ice that also contains salt. What new insights into Ceresâ salt deposits and water ice will researchers make in the coming years and decades?

articles.title: The Fake Photo That Helped Sink a U.S. Senator
articles.summary: The two men had never posed together, and the caption underneath called the picture a composite. To a picture editor, it meant two negatives combined.
articles.summary_short: The two men had never posed together, and the caption underneath called the picture a composite. To a picture editor, it meant two negatives combined.
articles.summary_long:
In the last stretch of the 1950 Maryland Senate race, roughly 300,000 copies of a four-page tabloid called From the Record went out across the state, and inside was a picture of Senator Millard Tydings standing close beside Earl Browder, the former head of the American Communist Party. The two men had never posed together, and the caption underneath called the picture a composite. What went into the Tydings picture were two real news photographs, and the Senate report is precise about them.

One was a 1938 photograph of Tydings, taken while he listened to election returns. The tabloid ran the word composite in the caption anyway. To a picture editor, it meant two negatives combined.

A composite disclosure is attached to a specific printed instance of an image. It does not tell you the picture is honest. If you sell a composite as a composite, say it in the visible caption, in the language a reader already speaks, and say what was combined.

Wildlife files need more editing than most genres because they come from long lenses at high ISOs, subjects that won't pose, and backgrounds you couldn't choose. The edits that rescue those frames, such as cropping, noise reduction, and masked brightening, are the same ones that most often push a photo past the point where it looks natural. Matt Kloskowski sees it constantly when he reviews wildlife images.

Kloskowski calls it uncomfortable, which fits how your eye reacts when a wingtip or tail touches the edge. When an adjustment costs nothing to apply, the limit has to come from your eye, because your patience no longer sets one. Kloskowski lands around 50% to 60% as a starting point.

Pulling it lower lets noise creep back into dark backgrounds, which is where it tends to be worst. The background stays clean, and the subject gets some bite back. Kloskowski then moves to what he calls the sticker effect, where the subject is brightened, or the background darkened, until the animal looks pasted onto the scene with perfect edges.

articles.summary_long:
“ Everything Twice ” is a quiet meditation on disability and the ways we orient ourselves in the world. Since childhood, Cy Kuckenbaker noticed that one of his eyes drooped, something he attributed to a snowboarding accident. But doctors quickly dismissed that theory, and after innumerable tests and many, many years, the photographer learned he was born with a rare disease.

Kuckenbaker chronicles this realization alongside a slow, analog process he began to combat burnout. Utilizing homemade cameras crafted from cardboard boxes and drugstore magnifying glasses, he captured a variety of landscapes and sights on the West Coast. Pairing both the slow processes of labor-intensive photography with that of uncovering an unusual ailment creates a short film that’s equal part self-discovery and contemplation on disconnection and loss.

articles.title: November’s Night Sky Notes: Light-Day Away
articles.summary: In 1977, NASA launched twin spacecraft Voyager 1 and 2, taking advantage of a once-every-175-year planetary alignment of the four largest planets in our solar system: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Additionally, track each Voyager spacecraft here .

articles.summary_long:
In 1977, NASA launched twin spacecraft Voyager 1 and 2, taking advantage of a once-every-175-year planetary alignment of the four largest planets in our solar system: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Using six gravity assists between them, this Grand Tour gave us up-close views of the gas and ice giants, including several moons. As Voyager 2 continued toward Uranus and Neptune, Voyager 1 grabbed one more portrait of the solar system (excluding Mercury and Mars), including a final image of the pale blue dot we call home.

Did you know that a light-minute is a measure of distance, not time? At the time of this article, the Canberra antenna tracked Voyager 1 at 25.80 billion km, or just over 16 billion miles. You may have heard the term light-year in your favorite sci-fi movie or show, or when stargazing and referring to an object outside of our solar system.

This video best demonstrates the different distances between the inner solar system, outer solar system, and beyond, using light measurements. Additionally, track each Voyager spacecraft here . You can get a real understanding of what a gravity assist might be like with our Gravity Assist activity and learn what it’s like to measure a “light minute” with our Measuring a Kid Minute activity guide!

These past few years haven’t been kind to photography blogs. Many of the old classic websites have gone offline, and others have changed almost to the point of being unrecognizable. Photography Life has managed to weather the storm successfully for a few reasons.

It’s our way of holding our own against some much larger companies even in a declining industry. But I still hope that we can stick around a little longer and keep sharing our stories from the world of photography with you. If you’re wondering about ways to help Photography Life stay afloat, there is one thing which helps more than anything else, and that’s joining our Member Page .

It’s not just a way to help us; I think you’ll find that it’s a valuable resource for your own photography, no matter what level of photographer you are. And if it makes a difference, I enabled our planned Black Friday sale a month early so that you don’t feel like you’re getting a bad deal if you join. But no matter what happens, I am so grateful to have had these past ten years to share my love for photography with you.

Viltrox has announced the AF 35mm f/1.4 Pro, a weather-sealed full frame prime for Sony E and Nikon Z with a 16-element optical design and voice coil autofocus. It costs $829 and joins the 50mm and 85mm f/1.4 Pro lenses, which gives Viltrox a set of three fast primes that comes in under $2,000 combined. In its launch announcement , Viltrox says the Viltrox AF 35mm f/1.4 Pro stays sharp to the corners wide open, and it uses 16 elements in 11 groups to get there.

Viltrox says it kept focus breathing to a minimum, which matters for video and also makes the lens a good fit for focus stacking. The Sony version weighs about 760 g, and the Nikon version weighs about 780 g. The 35mm fills the last gap in Viltrox's full frame Pro line.

The AF 85mm f/1.4 Pro sells for $598 and the AF 50mm f/1.4 Pro for $549, so the three lenses add up to $1,976, and if you already own the 50mm, the 35mm uses the same PL-68A lens hood. If you shoot both stills and video, the click switch lets you choose between detents for stills and a smooth aperture ring for video, the voice coil motors keep focus noise down, and the low breathing keeps focus pulls from visibly zooming the frame. The Viltrox AF 35mm f/1.4 Pro for Sony E and the Viltrox AF 35mm f/1.4 Pro for Nikon Z are available now for $829.

On July 10, 2013, Natalia Botero-Acosta photographed a humpback whale's tail going down in the Gulf of Tribugá, on Colombia's Pacific coast. On August 22, 2022, Ekaterina Kalashnikova photographed a fluke off Fumba, in the Zanzibar channel, on the far side of the planet. No photo-identified adult male humpback has been logged across a greater great-circle distance between two breeding grounds, and no individual had previously been recorded alternating breeding grounds between the Pacific and Indian Oceans.

Among the longest separations previously documented between two humpback sightings was 11,261 kilometers, between the Mariana Islands and Mexico, with a year in between. An off-axis fluke often still matches, and a whale you photographed badly is worth more than a whale you did not photograph. The underlying finding deserved the attention, because a male crossing between the breeding stocks of two different ocean basins is genuinely extraordinary and nobody had documented it between these two.

The number 13,046 is a great-circle distance: the shortest path across a sphere between two coordinates where a camera happened to be pointing at this whale. Two frames prove that one whale was in two places on two dates. Working through 19,283 curated photo-ID images collected between 1984 and 2025, the team found two humpbacks that had been photographed in both eastern Australia and Brazil, moving in both directions.

The spacecraft struck Dimorphos on 26 September 2022, travelling at about 6.1 kilometers per second. Before the collision, Dimorphos took about 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit Didymos. ESA expects the first detailed images of Dimorphos on 25 November 2026.

articles.summary: Le grand lieu consacré à la photographie que la Région Hauts-de-France prépare à Lille devra encore attendre. Selon La Voix du Nord , l’ Institut pour la photographie ne rouvrira pas avant début 2030 .

articles.summary_long:
Le grand lieu consacré à la photographie que la Région Hauts-de-France prépare à Lille devra encore attendre. Selon La Voix du Nord , l’ Institut pour la photographie ne rouvrira pas avant début 2030 . Sa réouverture était d’abord prévue pour 2026 , l’année du bicentenaire de la photographie.

En juin, la Région a mis fin à sa collaboration avec l’agence Berger & Berger , chargée de la rénovation, en invoquant une « défaillance ». Le projet a aussi été revu à la baisse : l’Institut occupera environ 2 600 m² , contre 3 900 m² prévus jusqu’ici. La Région parle d’un simple « contretemps ».

Pour ne pas rater complètement le bicentenaire de la photographie , célébré jusqu’en septembre 2027, la Région prévoit d’ouvrir provisoirement un petit espace de 270 m² sur place. D’ici là, l’Institut continue de travailler hors les murs, notamment au Théâtre du Nord. Olivier Spillebout , fondateur de la Maison de la Photographie de Lille, dénonce depuis plusieurs années le coût d’une institution financée depuis 2018 sans véritable lieu ouvert au public .

He calls it by far the best everyday pocketable camera you can buy in 2026, and part of his case is its size.

The rain, meanwhile, plays to one of his favorite subjects, reflections, with a puddle on Piccadilly giving him one as people with umbrellas walk through the frame. At Elizabeth Tower, he focuses manually through a puddle so the clock tower sits sharp in the reflection. He uses a longer exposure so people walking through the frame blur while the tower stays in focus.

What he demonstrates at Elizabeth Tower belongs to a broader technique called intentional camera movement, where you move the camera on purpose during the exposure to get abstract, painterly results. He doesn't present the camera as flawless. He calls the ISO 12,800 result very impressive and says he can't fault the camera in low light.

Explaining what makes a photograph good is another matter, because following steps X, Y, and Z doesn't guarantee a good image, and a technically awful photograph can still be an amazing one. For your own work, it helps to split what you learn into two piles. You can master that pile with practice and a little discipline.

The second pile holds what you can only train by looking: timing, gesture, what to leave out, and how one picture sits next to another. You build that pile slowly by studying printed work you admire, laying your own prints out on a table, and revisiting your selects months later when you've forgotten how it felt to take them. articles.summary_long:
Gretchen Scherer ’s paintings of affluent homes, studios, and libraries appear to expand before our eyes. Brimming with ornately framed paintings installed salon-style on richly papered walls, her half-imagined spaces are inspired by real places, which she infuses with a playful brightness and whimsy. When we home in on one particular floral arrangement, framed artwork, or piece of furniture, it seems that there’s a sudden increase in how much more there is to explore.

Scherer’s new solo exhibition, In Time at Monya Rowe Gallery , continues the artist’s fascination with historical interiors, from art museums and drawing rooms to palatial halls and ecclesiastical spaces. The artist leans into a kind of escapism or longing for not only elegant, luminous surroundings but a desire to immerse oneself, quite literally, in the world of art. In our era of steel, glass, concrete, and contractor gray interiors, Scherer celebrates craftsmanship and beauty.

Fantastical convergences of art history and architecture occur in pieces like “A French Cafe with Paintings,” where a Beaux Arts interior transforms into an ad hoc gallery with myriad famous works casually strewn about. Working in oil, Scherer’s choice of media nods to the same used to create many of the historical examples she includes. In Time opens today and continues through January 9 in New York.

We’ve seen some amazing costumes brought to life with maker skills. From moving masks and giant wings to a flickering cathedral dress , having a variety of techniques at your disposal can enable some truly original ideas. Still, I never expected to see a public transit fare gate costume before.

Taylor Waddell, who you might recognize from the OpenCAL layerless 3D printer , saw a BART gate and asked “why not?” It was largely constructed with a laser cutter at Jacob’s Makerspace at UC Berkeley, and features motorized doors and a working card reader. This is actually Waddell’s 2nd fare gate costume, built to reflect the changes in transit design since his earlier iteration. As it happens, there are actually has multiple BART mascots to emulate; from Baylee the online influencer who loves boba, to Barty “the reincarnated bunny spirit of a legacy car who has seen it all.” If you’re in the SF Bay Area and excited about showing your local public transportation pride, Waddell has just unleashed one more idea to choose from.

Les références des points de livraison d’électricité (PDL) et des points de comptage et d’estimation du gaz (PCE) figurent également parmi les informations exposées. Le groupe indique avoir interrompu les accès non autorisés. En s’appuyant sur des données personnelles et des références contractuelles exactes, des fraudeurs pourraient se faire passer pour des conseillers du fournisseur ou des techniciens afin d’obtenir des informations supplémentaires ou d’inciter les clients à effectuer des paiements frauduleux. Engie appelle ses clients à la vigilance face aux sollicitations inhabituelles.

articles.title: La Mutuelle Communale victime d'une fuite de données
articles.summary: Le groupe Blackhatsect0r affirme avoir dérobé les données de plus de 50 000 contacts et 114 214 documents PDF de La Mutuelle Communale. Les informations revendiquées comprennent notamment des numéros de Sécurité sociale, des adresses électroniques et des coordonnées bancaires.
articles.summary_short: Le groupe Blackhatsect0r affirme avoir dérobé les données de plus de 50 000 contacts et 114 214 documents PDF de La Mutuelle Communale. Les informations revendiquées comprennent notamment des numéros de Sécurité sociale, des adresses électroniques et des coordonnées bancaires.
articles.summary_long:
Le groupe Blackhatsect0r affirme avoir dérobé les données de plus de 50 000 contacts et 114 214 documents PDF de La Mutuelle Communale. Les informations revendiquées comprennent notamment des numéros de Sécurité sociale, des adresses électroniques et des coordonnées bancaires. Selon les chiffres rapportés le 27 octobre par le site Cyberattaque.org , les attaquants prétendent avoir récupéré 50 344 fiches de contacts et 114 214 documents PDF, représentant 46,6 Go de données.

Les données annoncées par les cybercriminels comprennent plusieurs catégories d’informations personnelles. BlackHatsect0r affirme notamment détenir 30 056 enregistrements de numéros de Sécurité sociale, dont 24 335 valeurs distinctes, ainsi que 17 812 enregistrements d’IBAN, dont 12 153 valeurs distinctes. Cyberattaque.org indique avoir examiné cinq extraits CSV de 1 000 enregistrements chacun, ainsi que plusieurs documents PDF.

Au-delà des données relatives aux adhérents, la revendication évoque plusieurs composants du système d’information. Selon le site Cyberattaque.org, Blackhatsect0r affirme proposer l’ensemble des données revendiquées à la vente pour 10 000€, avec un règlement en cryptomonnaie. La combinaison de coordonnées personnelles, de données bancaires et de documents administratifs pourrait faciliter des tentatives d’usurpation d’identité, de fraude documentaire ou d’hameçonnage ciblé.

articles.title: Avec le projet Lightwell, IBM et Red Hat gèrent les patchs des logiciels open source
articles.summary: Face à l'afflux attendu de correctifs de failles découvertes par l'IA sur les logiciels open source, IBM et Red Hat présentent le projet Lightwell. Cette plateforme combinant IA et expertise humaine sert de couche de coordination pour intégrer les patchs dans la supply chain logicielle des entreprises sans interruption de service.

articles.summary_long:
Face à l'afflux attendu de correctifs de failles découvertes par l'IA sur les logiciels open source, IBM et Red Hat présentent le projet Lightwell. Cette plateforme combinant IA et expertise humaine sert de couche de coordination pour intégrer les patchs dans la supply chain logicielle des entreprises sans interruption de service. Il revendiqué la découverte de plusieurs milliers de failles dans des applications open source.

Pour répondre à ces problématiques, IBM et sa filiale Red Hat viennent de présenter le projet Lightwell, doté d’un budget de 5 Md$ et mobilisant 20 000 ingénieurs des deux sociétés. L’objectif de l’initiative est de créer une plateforme pour accélérer la détection et la correction des vulnérabilités dans les logiciels open source. Aucune mise à niveau ni accès au code source n’est requis.

Les entreprises pourront partager des vulnérabilités sensibles sous embargo via un « modèle d'intermédiaire sécurisé » et recevoir des correctifs validés pour les plateformes Red Hat et le code de la communauté indépendante. Elles pourront également déployer des correctifs sur l'ensemble des chaînes de dépendances, signaler et résoudre les problèmes dans les environnements de production actifs, et partager les correctifs en amont afin que la communauté open source puisse les intégrer. « Nous voulons nous assurer que tous les correctifs que nous fournissons aux entreprises via la plateforme soient également mis à la disposition de la communauté open source qui a développé le code », explique Ashesh Badani, vice-président senior et directeur des produits chez Red Hat, à CSOonline .

articles.summary_long:
En rendant public sur un répertoire GitHub les principes mathématiques qui sous-tendent sa vérification du chiffrement post-quantique, Apple met au défi l'ensemble du secteur de prouver que son propre code est sûr. L'univers de la technologie prend rapidement conscience de la menace que représentent les futurs systèmes quantiques pour la sécurité au moment où ils seront capables de contourner facilement le chiffrement utilisé actuellement pour protéger sa présence sur Internet. Dans ce contexte, la décision d’Apple de partager le code de cryptographie post-quantique de l’iPhone et du Mac sur GitHub en dit long.

Les documents récemment publiés comprennent le code source de corecrypto, la bibliothèque cryptographique utilisée par le framework de sécurité d’Apple, CryptoKit et CommonCrypto. Cela fait des années que la firme à la pomme travaille sur la protection cryptographique post-quantique. Cette protection sécurise à la fois les conversations et leurs clés de chiffrement contre de futures attaques quantiques.

L’entreprise pense qu’en le publiant de cette manière, les chercheurs en sécurité pourront vraiment mettre ces protections à l'épreuve pour s'assurer qu'elles fonctionneront lorsque l'informatique quantique deviendra véritablement une menace. Le chiffrement post-quantique d’Apple présente toutefois des limites. Il est bon de voir qu’Apple continue ainsi de mettre en place des protections contre la menace imminente de l’informatique quantique.
